messages:
maya: FYI we're getting a support ticket — Dedicated console shows 0 GPUs for eu-west-2-cluster-7 after yesterday's rollback. API /inventory still returns 12 GPUs, prometheus shows node_gpu_count=12. Customers see capacity errors. :grimacing:

support-bot: New escalation opened: INC-5137, customer reported autoscale failing, their requests were routed to hostless pool. Link: https://support.example/inc/5137

olivia: Can you paste the exact cluster id and a screenshot? I want to rule out UI caching.

maya: cluster id: cluster-euw-7 (human name: eu-west-2-cluster-7). Screenshot attached in ticket (not in thread). I checked /api/v1/dedicated/cluster/cluster-euw-7/inventory -> returns JSON with nodes array length 4 and total_gpus: 12. UI shows "0 GPUs available" and empty node table.

kevin: @olivia will look at the console query. @raj can you check the inventory-indexer logs? Might be mismatch on cluster alias after the rename+rollback.

raj: Checking indexer logs now. quick grep:
```
kubectl -n infra logs deployment/inventory-indexer | tail -n 200 | grep cluster-euw-7
```
seeing: "WARN: alias not found for cluster-euw-7, skipping update" repeated lots. indexer last successful run: 2025-11-02T03:12:08Z then error loop.

olivia: UI queries go through /console/internal/cluster-mapping which resolves alias -> id. If alias not present it falls back to 0 counts. Suspect alias store in redis got a stale key after the rollback.

maya: I can repro locally: call console endpoint: `GET /console/internal/cluster-mapping?name=eu-west-2-cluster-7` returns `{"aliases": []}` but inventory API returns nodes. So two different sources disagree.

kevin: Possible root cause: during the rollback we temporarily renamed clusters (added suffix -rollback) then moved back; the alias backfill job didn't run. There's a backfill cronjob `inventory-alias-backfill` that is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.

raj: Confirmed. `kubectl -n infra get pods` shows `inventory-alias-backfill-0 CrashLoopBackOff`. Logs show `KeyError: 'cluster_aliases'` in the first attempt. Looks like a schema migration didn't finish.

olivia: Quick mitigation: repoint the console to use the inventory API for the UI query until backfill is fixed. Short term: add a fallback in the UI config (feature flag) `console.use_inventory_fallback=true` — can we flip that?

kevin: I can flip the flag in prod config -> doing it now. patch in console-config: `PATCH /api/v1/config/console {"use_inventory_fallback":true}`. Will roll in 30s.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: config change applied by kevin at 2026-03-17T12:34:10Z, rollout to 3 regions.

maya: After the flag flip the UI shows 12 GPUs, node table populated. I pinged the customer and asked for verification. They confirmed immediate improvement. :white_check_mark:

raj: Next steps: 1) fix alias-backfill job (schema migration), 2) run `scripts/backfill/alias_backfill.py --cluster cluster-euw-7` to recover aliases for all affected clusters, 3) add healthcheck + alert for alias-backfill CrashLoopBackOff. I'll open a PR for the migration fix.

kevin: Adding follow-up tasks in eng-sre board. Also scheduling a controlled run of backfill at 13:00 UTC to avoid load spikes.

olivia: For the postmortem include: timeline of rename/rollback, why schema migration didn't detect version mismatch, and why UI had no fallback before.

maya: Filing a brief escalation note into INC-5137 with link to this thread and the mitigation steps.

support-bot: INC-5137 updated: mitigation applied, customer notified.

maya: Leaving this thread open until backfill completes. Thanks all. :pray:
